data.headline: Two- and ten-year yields hold steady after Friday’s decline
data.summary: The two-year Treasury yield ended Monday at 4.63% and the ten-year at 4.92%, both level with Friday. The thirty-year yield edged down two basis points to 5.29%.

bull.text: The rise in bond prices implied by Monday’s yield decline was concentrated at the long end. The thirty-year benchmark eased from 5.31% on November 20 to 5.29% on November 23.

bear.text: Borrowers watching the ten-year benchmark saw no further easing on Monday. Its spread over the two-year held at 29 basis points.

watch.text: The thirty-year yield ended 37 basis points above the ten-year, down from 39 on Friday. The next release will show whether that gap narrows further.

limitations: Treasury reports constant-maturity par yields. These benchmark levels measure borrowing conditions and do not establish the return or direction of a stock index.
